chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man who performed Dhihar (verbal divorce) then had intercourse before expiating, so he said to me: 'Is it not thus that the jurist acts?'.

The meaning of this hadith is that if Dhihar is conditional upon intercourse, then the expiation is not obligatory except after penetration. So if he expiated before penetration, it would not be sufficient for what becomes obligatory upon him after penetration, and it would be incumbent upon him another expiation if he penetrated. So the Imam (peace be upon him) drew attention to the fact that intercourse, for one whose ruling is this, is from the actions of the jurist who seeks release from the obligation of another expiation upon him, and that is not except by intercourse. And that which also indicates that whoever whose Dhihar is absolute, not conditional, and he had intercourse before expiation, upon him are two expiations.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on expiation for Dhihar if the husband has intercourse before paying it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the timing of Kaffarah for Dhihar, distinguishing between conditional and absolute verbal divorces. He highlights that for conditional Dhihar, expiation is only obligatory after intercourse, meaning pre-intercourse payment is insufficient to prevent a second obligation. This ruling underscores the juristic precision required in Shia fiqh regarding the linkage between the act of intercourse and the validity of expiation.
